evidence.supports: The town's official, currently published list of zoning bylaw amendments shows only the September 2025 Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers among 2025 amendments and no 2026 entries, confirming no permanent data center bylaw has been adopted as of this research pass.

decisions.notes: The moratorium's own text set an end date of 2026-06-30. Because the anticipated permanent bylaw amendment was never placed on the 2026 ATM warrant (contrary to the Planning Board's earlier stated intent), the moratorium should be recorded as expired rather than active. Secondary reporting (thelocallens.org, a locally-run outlet whose meeting recaps are explicitly AI-generated and self-flagged as potentially inaccurate) had indicated the Planning Board was considering tabling the bylaw amid community opposition in spring 2026, which is consistent with this outcome, but that source was not relied on for the core finding -- the primary-source warrant/minutes and the official zoning-amendments page were.

current_status.to: Adopted. The Everett City Council enrolled the Section 37 (Docklands Innovation District) zoning amendment on 2026-06-08 and ordained (finally passed) it on 2026-06-22, converting data centers from a by-right to a restricted use with a combined footprint/power cap (the lesser of 20,000 square feet or 5 megawatts), required closed-loop cooling, funding of electric-system upgrades, backup generators, a minimum setback from housing, and a resident hiring preference.
current_status.reason: Advocate News (fetched directly) reports both the June 8, 2026 enrollment vote and the June 22, 2026 ordainment vote, along with the substance of the adopted restrictions.

outcome.from: Proposed shift from by-right treatment to special permit, ancillary-use limits, and size/capacity cap; no moratorium identified.
outcome.to: Adopted as a standing city ordinance amendment to Section 37 (not a moratorium -- no fixed sunset); restricts, rather than bans, data center development within the Docklands Innovation District.
outcome.reason: Advocate News confirms the amendment was ordained (finally passed), not merely proposed, and describes it as a standing zoning restriction rather than a time-limited moratorium.

evidence.title: City Council approves limits on data centers in Innovation District
evidence.supports: Establishes the June 8, 2026 (enrollment/first reading) and June 22, 2026 (ordainment/final passage) City Council votes and the substantive terms of the adopted Section 37 zoning amendment restricting data centers.
evidence.quote: Data centers will be limited to 20,000 combined vertical and horizontal square feet and five megawatts of power. Whichever number is smaller will take precedence.

decisions.notes: This is a city-council-enacted zoning ordinance amendment (Everett is a city with home-rule ordinance power acting on its own initiative, not a town meeting bylaw), so it is not subject to the Massachusetts Attorney General review under M.G.L. c.40A section 32 that applies to town-meeting-adopted zoning bylaws. I could not retrieve the official council agenda packet (an image-based PDF whose text could not be extracted) or the council's own minutes directly, so this rests on a single directly-fetched news account; a second outlet (Everett Independent) separately reported a 7-3 first-reading tally with named councilors, but I did not independently re-fetch and verify that article, so I have not relied on the specific vote count in this decision.

evidence.quote: Create a new Section 18, Building-Integrated Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and Data Centers to establish a one-year moratorium on Building-Integrated Energy Storage Systems (BESS) having an aggregate energy capacity equal to or greater than 50 kWh and less than 100 MWh and establish a one-year moratorium on Data Centers, in order to provide the Planning Board with sufficient time to study, consider, and adopt zoning regulations governing the siting, permitting, construction, installation, operation, and maintenance of the same.

decisions.notes: The Article 7 moratorium proposal is confirmed verbatim from the official warrant, and the 2026-06-29 Special Town Meeting warrant (also directly reviewed) contains only OPEB, Riverside Municipal Building roof, and stabilization-fund articles -- no data center or BESS item -- so no second bite at Article 7 was taken there. However, Gill has not published minutes or a results document for the May 4 / June 8, 2026 Annual Town Meeting as of 2026-07-31, and the only news coverage located (Recorder, covering both sessions) discussed only the school roof bond, budget, and a wood chipper purchase. Whether Article 7 passed, failed, or was tabled could not be determined from any source I could access. Recommend a direct records request to the Gill Town Clerk for the certified 2026 ATM minutes.
